title: On the VMS Word Length Distribution
summary: Stolfi counted distinct spellings and their occurrences separately in running text and labels. Counting each spelling once gave similar, nearly symmetric length distributions in the two samples. He illustrated how a codebook could produce that shape and identified manuscript features his example leaves unexplained.
established: The counts use a majority-vote transcription and Currier-style symbol lengths. Stolfi excluded words containing rare, unreadable or unresolved characters.

Figures 1–3 show that the length distributions for distinct spellings in text and labels are similar and close to one plus a binomial variable with nine trials at probability one half. Counting every occurrence gives different profiles for text and labels.

The illustrative nine-bit code records the positions of set bits and adds a marker. Its maximum length is ten. The published text table includes nine distinct spellings of length eleven and three of length twelve.

open.question: Can a codebook explain repeated glyphs and mutually exclusive gallows within words without a visible end marker?
open.check: Specify an encoding in advance and compare its predictions for repetitions, gallows co-occurrence and word boundaries with the transcription.
